# uptimeify_api_token (Resource)

An organization API token (`wsm_...`, full organization access unless `customer_id` is set). Only a signed-in organization admin can create, list or revoke these: the API answers API-token requests on `/api/organization/tokens` with 401, so with the provider's `wsm_` token every operation fails with a clear error until the API accepts tokens there. Use `uptimeify_customer_api_token` for customer-scoped tokens. The token value is returned once, on create, and kept in the state as a sensitive value; it cannot be read again, so an imported token has no `token`. Every change creates a new token. Import with the numeric id.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Note: the API only lets a signed-in admin manage organization tokens; with a wsm_ provider
# token this resource fails with an explanatory error.
resource "uptimeify_api_token" "ci" {
  name            = "CI pipeline"
  expires_in_days = 90
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)

### Optional

- `customer_id` (Number) Restrict the token to this customer. Unset = whole organization.
- `expires_in_days` (Number) Lifetime in days from creation. Unset = never expires. Only sent on create (not readable; see `expires_at`).

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `expires_at` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `last_used_at` (String)
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The token itself. Only known after create; empty after import.
- `token_hint` (String) Short recognition hint shown in the dashboard.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Numeric token id (the token value cannot be imported)
terraform import uptimeify_api_token.ci 15
```
